correctness.rationale: For m>=4,r>=1, no initial pair can start a forcing process spanning the hub and rim, whereas every hub-plus-adjacent-rim triple succeeds. An all-rim minimum triple must begin with a contiguous rim pair; before the hub turns blue, a white hub blocks spoke-to-rim forces. The only way the third seed can permit a spoke to color the hub is the explicitly classified near-spoke A or B pattern. Conversely each such triple colors the hub and then all rim vertices. The exact list has m(3r+2) distinct triples. Their one-token exchanges are exactly pair intersections: the m(r+1) hub triples form an induced rim cycle and all other triples attach to it. A finite pair-multiplicity table for every k type, with symmetry, determines degrees and m(6r+5) edges by handshaking; each case can be verified directly from the A/B/H formulas. The separate standalone checker exhausts all 2- and 3-vertex initial sets for 30 parameter pairs m=4..8,r=1..6 (164295 candidate triples) and checks all counts/adjacencies, but finite checks are not substituted for the general proof.

value.rationale: Generalized gears are canonical cyclic graphs with a hub and evenly spaced spokes. Moving between distinct minimum sensor/driver seed sets by a single replacement while never losing eventual forcing is a mathematically motivated constraint not determined by Z=3 or by propagation time. An explicit connected backbone, every local exchange degree, and exact edge and vertex counts provide a structural description of the full optimal solution space for infinitely many instances. The contribution is more than renaming a scalar invariant; prior descriptions do not give its feasible exchange graph.
